skill.name: convex-seed
skill.description: Create repeatable Convex database seed workflows with internal mutations or CLI imports that match schema validators.
skill.summary: Build idempotent Convex seed and import workflows for fixtures and bulk data.
skill.author: get-convex

security_audit.summary: All three static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks around documented Convex CLI commands. SKILL.md contains workflow guidance only, includes no executable shell code, and explicitly warns against seeding secrets or PII.

static_findings.snippet: Populate tables via an internalMutation seed function (re-runnable) or `npx convex import`, matching
1. For fixtures: write an internalMutation that inserts sample rows; run it with `npx convex run`.
2. For bulk import: shape the data to the schema and use `npx convex import`.

finding_verdicts.reason: The backticks delimit the documented `npx convex import` command in Markdown. SKILL.md contains instructions only and does not execute this command or interpolate user input.
The backticks format `npx convex run` as inline Markdown. There is no Ruby code, shell script, execution primitive, or dynamic command construction.
The line documents the fixed `npx convex import` CLI command in an ordered workflow. It does not contain executable code or an unsanitized command injection path.

content.value_statement: Preparing reliable fixtures and bulk data for Convex can require repetitive schema checks and careful reruns. This skill guides idempotent internal mutations and CLI imports.
actual_capabilities: Guides internalMutation seed functions that insert sample rows matching schema validators.
Explains bulk data preparation for the Convex import command.
Recommends clear-then-insert or upsert patterns for repeatable seeding.
Provides the Convex CLI command for running an internal seed mutation.
Includes row count verification after seeding or importing data.
limitations: Requires an existing Convex project, schema, and configured CLI access.
Does not provide bundled scripts, fixture files, or generated sample data.
Does not document import formats, CLI options, rollback procedures, or deployment selection.
Does not replace review of sensitive data before using a shared deployment.

use_cases.title: Prepare Local Fixtures
use_cases.description: Create repeatable sample records for local feature development and testing.

use_cases.title: Import Existing Data
use_cases.description: Shape a bulk dataset to match Convex validators before importing it.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Seeding
use_cases.description: Define an idempotent seed workflow with verification for shared development environments.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Fixtures
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Convex internalMutation that seeds sample rows for [table]. Match these validators: [schema]. Make reruns safe.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start a small fixture set for local development.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Bulk Import
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a Convex bulk import for [dataset]. Compare its fields with [schema], identify required transformations, and include row count verification.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare existing data for a Convex table.

prompt_templates.title: Make Seeding Idempotent
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Convex seed workflow: [workflow]. Choose clear-then-insert or upsert, explain the choice, and prevent duplicate records.
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve a seed process that may run repeatedly.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Multi-Table Seed Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an idempotent Convex seed workflow for these related tables: [tables and schemas]. Preserve dependencies, avoid sensitive data, and verify each table count.
prompt_templates.scenario: Coordinate advanced fixtures across related tables.

output_examples.input: Create repeatable fixtures for users and projects.
output: Seed users before projects so project references resolve correctly.
Use stable identifiers or an upsert strategy to prevent duplicates.
Verify user and project row counts after the mutation completes.

output_examples.input: Prepare a customer export for Convex import.
output_examples.output: A field-mapping plan that aligns source columns with Convex validators, excludes sensitive values, runs the import, and verifies the final row count.

output_examples.input: Fix a seed process that duplicates records.
output_examples.output: An idempotent workflow using either clear-then-insert for disposable fixtures or upsert for records that must remain stable.

best_practices: Match every seeded or imported field to the current Convex validators.
Use clear-then-insert or upsert so rerunning the workflow remains predictable.
Verify row counts and review the target deployment after each operation.
anti_patterns: Do not seed secrets or personal data into a shared deployment.
Do not use append-only inserts when the workflow must support reruns.
Do not import data before checking field shapes against schema validators.

faq.question: What seeding methods does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers internalMutation fixture functions and bulk imports through the Convex CLI.

faq.question: Can I rerun the generated seed workflow?
faq.answer: Yes, when it uses clear-then-insert or upsert as recommended.

faq.question: Does this skill generate fixture data?
faq.answer: It can guide fixture design, but the skill does not include ready-made fixture files.

faq.question: Will it validate my data automatically?
faq.answer: No. It instructs the agent to match your schema, but you must provide and review the validators.

faq.question: Can I use it with a production deployment?
faq.answer: The workflow can target configured deployments, but production imports require independent review, backups, and careful access controls.

faq.question: How does it protect sensitive data?
faq.answer: It explicitly prohibits seeding secrets or personal data into shared deployments. You remain responsible for reviewing source data.
